text:
Kenji S.: Heads-up team — were publishing a coordinated docs + samples change: the quickstart sections across languages are being rewritten to use the reproducible example kit and the old `start-local` devserver is being deprecated.
Aria M.: whats the reason?
Kenji S.: two reasons: 1) the inline quickstarts often drift and silently break; 2) `start-local` encouraged local-only hacks that mask cloud behavior (auth, model routing). New approach: single canonical sample repo (rw-examples) with pinned Docker dev images, CI-validated examples, and a tiny CLI `rw-kit` to fetch and run reproducible quickstarts.
docs-bot: New guide + repo: https://docs.redwood.ai/docs/quickstart-rewrite (rw-examples, rw-kit usage, CI recipes)
Felix R.: timeline & impact?
Kenji S.: Deprecation notice goes live now. Docs will switch visible quickstarts to point to rw-examples next week. `start-local` deprecation: 30-day grace period, then the devserver binary will be removed from published SDK packages. Were keeping a compatibility wrapper `start-local-legacy` for teams that need extra time, but it wont be maintained long-term.
Samira T.: examples for teams that want zero-change?
Kenji S.: Two options: 1) pin the SDK version that still includes start-local (example below) 2) use `start-local-legacy` container from our internal registry (documented link). Pin snippet:

```
# python requirements.txt
redwood-sdk==3.22.0

# node package.json
"dependencies": {
  "@redwood/inference": "3.22.0"
}

# Warning: this includes start-local which is deprecated. Plan to migrate to rw-kit.
```

Aria M.: how do teams migrate quickly?
Kenji S.: recommended path: 1) run `rw-kit sync` to fetch the language quickstart for your repo 2) run the example with the pinned docker image: `rw-kit run --lang=python --image=rw/dev:2026-02-01` 3) add `rw-kit validate` to CI which runs the example smoke tests. We also provide codemods to convert old config keys (e.g., `local_port` -> `dev_port`) and a sample GH Action.
docs-bot: Codemod + GH Action snippets included in the guide.
Felix R.: CI snippet?
Kenji S.: Example GH Action step: `- name: Validate quickstart
  run: |
    pip install rw-kit && rw-kit validate --path=docs/quickstart --matrix=python,node`

Samira T.: any telemetry or signals to help prioritize migration?
Kenji S.: We shipped an opt-in scanner that fingerprints usage of `start-local` and associated config keys (no request payloads). Playbook includes a BigQuery query teams can run to estimate affected repos.
Aria M.: private/dedicated customers — any difference?
Kenji S.: For Dedicated customers we added a console toggle that temporarily maps the rw-examples docker image to a customer-hosted mirror. Private/on-prem customers can request an offline bundle with the legacy devserver for 60 days. Details in the migration doc.
Felix R.: who to ping if quickstarts break during the switchover?
Kenji S.: Ping me (@kenji) or Aria in #docs, or open an issue in `docs-infra` with label `quickstart-migration`. Well triage high-severity breakages and can open an emergency compatibility mirror if needed.
Samira T.: TL;DR?
Kenji S.: 1) Quickstarts will point to rw-examples next week 2) start-local deprecated, 30-day grace then removal from packages 3) use rw-kit + pinned Docker images for reproducible dev 4) add rw-kit validate to CI 5) opt-in scanner + console flags for Dedicated/Private 6) ping #docs or open `quickstart-migration` issues for blockers.
docs-bot: Migration guide, codemods, and reproducible kit: https://docs.redwood.ai/docs/quickstart-rewrite#migration
Aria M.: thanks  Ill schedule the codemod dry-run on our repos and add the validate step to the docs CI.
